proposals.title: Multi-Scale Spatial Domain Discovery via Graph-Based Clustering
proposals.summary: This analysis identifies tissue domains by jointly leveraging gene expression and spatial coordinates across multiple scales. By constructing a spatial neighborhood graph and performing unsupervised clustering at both local and global resolutions, the method reveals coherent anatomical regions while mitigating the loss of spatial continuity. The approach incorporates rigorous quality control and sensitivity analysis to optimize graph connectivity, addressing technical variability and ensuring that the derived domains reflect biologically relevant microenvironments as expected in the hidden study.

proposals.title: Serial Section Alignment and Multi-Sample Registration
proposals.summary: This proposal centers on the spatial registration and alignment of serial tissue sections collected from different samples or platforms. Using landmark-based spatial registration and integrated quality control measures, the analysis merges data across slices to create a cohesive representation of tissue architecture. This enables robust cross-section comparisons and ensures that subsequent spatial domain and differential expression analyses incorporate the full structural context, in line with the spatial-omics goals of the hidden paper.

proposals.title: Spatially Informed Cell Type Deconvolution with Graph Context
proposals.summary: This analysis focuses on deconvolving mixed cell type signals at each spatial capture spot by integrating external single-cell transcriptomic references with spatial graph information. By leveraging both gene expression patterns and neighborhood structures, the method estimates the contribution of distinct cell types or states within spatially heterogeneous regions. This spatially aware deconvolution not only enhances interpretation of mixed signals but also ensures that the resulting cell type annotations are consistent with underlying tissue morphology, addressing a key gap highlighted in the critique.

proposals.title: Joint Expression–Spatial Representation Learning
proposals.summary: Utilizing modern representation learning, this proposal develops joint embeddings that capture both molecular profiles and spatial organization. This approach employs contrastive and graph neural network methods to learn latent representations that reflect local cellular neighborhoods and global tissue structures. The learned representations facilitate downstream tasks such as domain delineation, deconvolution, and anomaly detection, thereby aligning with the paper’s ambition to integrate histological context with expression data.

proposals.title: Advanced Quality Control and Spatial Artifact Correction
proposals.summary: This analysis enhances traditional quality control pipelines by incorporating spatial bias detection and correction. It systematically screens for low-quality spots and spatial artifacts using signal intensity measures and local spatial autocorrelation statistics. Subsequent filtering and normalization ensure that both molecular and geometric data are reliable for integrative analyses, making the workflow robust against technical variability and better suited for uncovering true biological signals.

proposals.title: Integrative Batch Correction and Multi-Platform Harmonization
proposals.summary: Recognizing the challenges of combining datasets across platforms and experimental batches, this proposal implements integrative batch correction strategies designed for spatial transcriptomics. The analysis aligns data from different sources using both gene expression profiles and spatial landmark registration, ensuring that real biological differences are preserved while technical variability is minimized. This harmonization is essential for joint analysis of serial sections and heterogeneous tissues, echoing the hidden paper's aims.

proposals.title: Neighborhood Graph Sensitivity Analysis for Robust Domain Definition
proposals.summary: Focusing on the reliability of spatial domain identification, this analysis systematically evaluates the sensitivity of spatial neighborhood graphs to differing connectivity parameters. Through iterative testing and validation against known anatomical features, the method refines clustering thresholds to robustly delineate biologically meaningful regions. This rigorous approach addresses concerns regarding over- or under-clustering, ensuring that the spatial domains faithfully convey true tissue structures.

proposals.title: Spatial Differential Expression with Contextual Neighborhood Scoring
proposals.summary: This proposal enhances traditional differential expression analyses by incorporating spatial context into the statistical framework. By weighting gene expression differences using information from surrounding neighborhoods, the analysis pinpoints genes that are not only differentially expressed but also relevant within the local tissue microenvironment. This method bridges the gap between molecular and spatial analyses, providing a comprehensive view of tissue heterogeneity that aligns with the study's objectives.

proposals.title: Hierarchical Clustering of Tissue Microenvironments
proposals.summary: This analysis employs hierarchical clustering methods to capture multi-layered tissue organization, from broad anatomical domains to finer microenvironments. By integrating both spatial metrics and molecular signatures, the approach identifies nested structures within the tissue. This comprehensive framework supports detailed interpretation of tissue organization and allows for comparisons across scales, reflecting the complex biological patterns likely explored in the hidden paper.

proposals.title: Integrated Single-Cell Reference Mapping for Spatial Annotation
proposals.summary: Leveraging external single-cell transcriptomic datasets, this method maps high-resolution cell type annotations onto spatial transcriptomics data. The approach combines reference-based deconvolution with spatial registration techniques to assign cellular identities to mixed spots, thereby enhancing both the resolution and interpretability of spatial heterogeneity. This integration ensures that single-cell insights are successfully transferred to the spatial domain, fulfilling a key goal outlined in the hidden study.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analyses most likely performed in the hidden paper, using a three-step TA+CV workflow that produces draft, critique, and final proposal JSON artifacts.

steps.title: Draft spatial analysis proposal set
steps.description: Use the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) to generate an initial, machine-readable draft set of exactly 10 distinct computational spatial-omics analysis proposals grounded solely in the provided public background (e.g., spatial domains, multi-section alignment, spatially informed deconvolution, and joint expression–geometry representations). The agent should not execute any analyses, only describe them, and must physically write the draft artifact to `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` in a structured JSON format suitable for downstream critique and synthesis.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial-CV planning step provides a focused, domain-aware exploration of plausible analyses for the hidden paper, incorporating spatial structure and cross-validation thinking without running experiments. This establishes a concrete, editable proposal set that later agents can critique and refine, while satisfying the requirement that the Recruiter assign this step specifically to `spatial_cv_agent` and that the artifact be written to the exact draft path.
steps.assignment_rationale: The spatial_cv_agent is explicitly required for the TA+CV treatment and is specialized for drafting exactly 10 spatial-paper analyses, producing the draft proposals artifact needed for downstream critique and synthesis.

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Use a critique-focused agent (e.g., a Critic agent) to read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and produce a structured critique of the 10 draft proposals, assessing coverage of the problem space implied by the public background, redundancy between proposals, feasibility, interpretability, and alignment with spatial-omics and representation-learning goals. The agent must not alter the draft file or execute any analyses, and must physically write its critique to `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` once the draft artifact exists.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated critique step provides quality control over the initial proposal set, identifying gaps, overlaps, and potential misalignments before final synthesis. This mirrors TA+CV-style separation between proposal generation and evaluation, and the explicit critique artifact enables the final synthesis agent to make traceable, justified adjustments while respecting the requirement that the Critic’s only output be the specified critique file.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is purpose-built to review and critique candidate spatial paper analyses and is the only agent that advertises producing a critique artifact, matching the requirements for writing hypotheses/critique.json without generating proposals.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Use a hypothesis-synthesis agent (e.g., a Hypothesis or proposal-synthesis agent) to combine `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` into a refined, non-redundant final set of exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analysis proposals. The agent must not execute any analyses. It must physically write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, mapping to an array of exactly 10 items; each item must contain only `title` and a detailed `summary` describing the proposed analysis, its spatial-omics rationale, and its relation to the paper’s likely goals, without introducing any additional fields.
steps.reasoning: This synthesis step turns the critiqued draft into the single required deliverable in the precise format requested, ensuring there are exactly 10 well-motivated, distinct proposals suitable for the hidden paper context. By strictly enforcing the output schema and not running any analyses, it cleanly separates design from execution while honoring all path and structural constraints on `final_proposals.json`.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is designed for drafting and final synthesis of exactly 10 spatial analysis proposals and can transform the critiqued draft into the required final_proposals.json object with the specified schema.

provenance.justification: No existing plan template fits this highly constrained three-step TA+CV proposal-generation workflow, which must use specific agents (including `spatial_cv_agent`), fixed artifact paths, and a custom JSON structure without adding extra steps; therefore, the plan was written from scratch.
